children: on Thursday announced that its intravitreal injection remigromig for diabetic macular edema, a major cause of vision loss in diabetes, succeeded in a Phase 2b/3 trial, showing a similar level of efficacy to ranibizumab, a DME therapy marketed by Roche as Lucentis.

Citing topline data, the New Jersey-headquartered pharma giant said remigromig reached the primary endpoint in its pivotal Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO trial, with both doses under investigation showing non-inferiority to ranibizumab at 52 weeks.

BRUNELLO, the first of a pair of Phase 2b/3 trials testing remigromig, enrolled nearly 1,000 adults with DME to evaluate 0.5 mg and 0.8 mg doses of the trispecific antibody versus 0.5 mg of ranibizumab. Its primary endpoint was the mean change in best-corrected visual acuity, a measurement of visual acuity from baseline to week 52.
Both remigromig doses undergoing the study were well tolerated by patients, Merck
said, adding that the company plans to present the data at the American Academy of Ophthalmology Annual

title: Merck’s diabetic macular edema therapy succeeds in Phase 2b/3 trial
